principles.summary: An action is not executable merely because a capability exists; execution-time policy must positively permit it.
principles.gap: MADO has capability-selection policy and bounded MCP tools, but no universal execution-time action policy gate.

principles.summary: Explicit refusal must win over broader permission.
principles.gap: No shared action-policy vocabulary currently models deny-before-allow precedence.

principles.summary: A policy evaluation error must refuse rather than widen authority.
principles.gap: MADO rejects invalid capability metadata, but has no execution-time rule evaluator whose failures are defined as refusal.

principles.summary: The decision record must exist before the side effect is dispatched.
principles.gap: MADO has a durable event ledger, but not a single action gateway proving every future side effect has a pre-dispatch decision receipt.

principles.summary: Policy should decide on server-resolved target facts, not model-supplied labels or descriptions.
principles.gap: Stale Human Gate IDs are reread and rejected, but a generic action target-resolution contract does not exist.

principles.summary: An external MCP tool not positively known to be read-only is treated as a write.
principles.gap: MADO correctly annotates its own five MCP tools, but does not yet govern arbitrary external MCP tool effects.

principles.summary: An approved action must be re-resolved and revalidated immediately before execution.
principles.gap: Human Gate resolution validates current Gate identity, but arbitrary targets, grants and policy are not yet revalidated under a generic action contract.

principles.summary: A declined or already-pending equivalent write is not silently retried in the same conversational context.
principles.gap: MADO does not yet compute stable action equivalence digests across retries.

principles.summary: Whose authority is used and what caused the run are independent policy dimensions.
principles.gap: Cockpit events have actor strings, but there is no first-class initiator kind for person, schedule, automation or system replay.

principles.summary: While a person has taken control of a computer/session, automated actions are refused rather than queued.
principles.gap: MADO has Human Question Gates but no human-control lease/fence for interactive browser or computer takeover.

principles.summary: Governance rules can be evaluated and audited without enforcing them, to observe real traffic before promotion.
principles.gap: No shadow policy mode exists for future action rules.
